get.description: Retrieve the status of a snapshot request. Use the ID returned when the snapshot was requested: `snapshotStatusId` for CRM object snapshots, or `id` for bulk snapshots.

parameters.name: statusId
parameters.description: The ID returned when the snapshot was requested (`snapshotStatusId` or the bulk snapshot `id`).

post.description: Capture the current state of up to 200 CRM objects. Each snapshot is written to your journal as a `SNAPSHOT` entry, and its progress can be checked with the status endpoint using the returned `snapshotStatusId`. This operation is exempt from daily and ten-secondly rate limits.

post.summary: Trigger a bulk snapshot of data for a given account and object type.
post.description: Start an asynchronous snapshot of all CRM objects of one type in an account that has installed your app. Results are written to your journal as `SNAPSHOT` entries, and the returned `id` can be passed to the status endpoint to check progress. Limited to 2 requests per day for each account and object type.

get.description: Retrieve a list of webhook journal subscriptions. This endpoint provides access to subscription details without pagination, allowing you to view all current subscriptions in a single request. It is useful for managing and reviewing webhook subscriptions for your app.

post.description: Create a subscription, or update the existing one with the same subscription type, object type, and account. The request body sets which actions and objects are recorded in your journal.
Add a filter to a subscription. When a subscription has filters, only events that match at least one of them are recorded in your journal.

get.description: Retrieve the filters associated with a specific webhook subscription. This endpoint allows you to view the filters applied to a subscription, which can help in managing and understanding the conditions set for webhook events.

parameters.name: subscriptionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the subscription for which to retrieve filters. This is an integer value.

get.description: Retrieve a specific filter associated with a webhook journal subscription. This endpoint allows you to access the details of the filter identified by the filterId, which is useful for managing and understanding the conditions applied to webhook events.

parameters.name: filterId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the filter to retrieve. It is an integer value.

delete.description: Remove a specific filter from the webhooks journal subscriptions. This operation is useful for managing and cleaning up filters that are no longer needed. Once deleted, the filter cannot be recovered.

parameters.name: filterId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the filter to delete.

delete.description: Delete all of your app's subscriptions for an account, along with their filters. Changes in that account are no longer recorded in your journal.

parameters.name: portalId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the portal for which the webhook journal subscription is to be deleted.

get.description: Retrieve details of a specific webhook subscription using its unique identifier. This endpoint is useful for obtaining information about a particular subscription, such as its actions, object type, and associated properties.

parameters.name: subscriptionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the subscription to retrieve.

delete.description: Delete a specific webhook journal subscription using its unique identifier. This operation is useful for managing and cleaning up subscriptions that are no longer needed in your HubSpot account.

parameters.name: subscriptionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the subscription to delete. It must be provided as an integer.

inputs.description: The offsets (UUIDs) of the journal entries to fetch, up to 100 per request. Use the `currentOffset` values returned by other journal endpoints. If any value is not a valid UUID, the whole request is rejected with a `400`. Offsets that can't be fetched, including ones with no matching entry for your app (or for `installPortalId` when it is set), don't fail the request: each one appears in `errors` with the offset in `context.offset`, and `numErrors` counts them. An empty list returns an empty result.
